abstract: Transcription is a bursty, stochastic process. How transcriptional regulators reshape bursting dynamics during cellular responses remains poorly understood, largely because most single-cell RNA sequencing experiments measure only steady-state RNA abundance. Here, we present buRst, a probabilistic framework that infers burst frequency, burst size, and RNA degradation rates from metabolically labeled single-cell RNA sequencing (scSLAM-seq) during acute perturbations, without assuming steady state. It jointly models labeling measurements and RNA dynamics, propagating uncertainty from sparse labeling data into kinetic estimates. We applied buRst to acute MYC depletion in two melanoma cell lines. MYC amplified burst size in a manner scaling with its promoter occupancy, whereas it reduced burst frequency genome-wide, independently of occupancy. As a result, only strongly bound genes showed net activation, reconciling models of MYC as a selective activator and as a global amplifier of transcription.
